title: Sparse-session burst econ + latency mosaic (text charts)
content:
Summary:
This note documents a small set of text-mode benchmarks exploring the cost/latency tradeoffs for "sparse session" workloads: many sessions with few tokens each, bursty arrival patterns, and a high ratio of cold-to-warm sessions. The aim is to surface qualitative behaviors (amortization, slot fragmentation, prewarm penalty) across three representative server configs and two model variants. This is intended as a lightweight collateral piece to use in product discussions and an appendix for the sessionization playbook.

Key questions:
- How does session sparsity (mean tokens/session) affect dollars-per-query (DPQ) at p50/p95 latency SLOs?
- What is the marginal cost of lowering median latency from 150ms to 80ms under bursty arrival?
- How much headroom does an H100 node provide vs A100 for sparse bursts when KV cache hit rates are low?

Experimental setup (short):
- Workload generator: in-house synthetic harness (bench/sparse-driver) that models Poisson bursts (peak QPS short windows) and a session mix: 70% short (<=8 tokens), 20% medium (9-64 tokens), 10% long (>64 tokens).
- Models: Model-A (open-13B quant4 general-purpose), Model-B (open-7B q4f16 optimized). Both served with our runtime with continuous batching and KV cache options enabled.
- HW profiles: 1x A100-40GB, 1x H100-80GB, and a tiny dedicated-pool profile (2xA100 but slot-isolated).
- Configuration: batcher max_batch=64, max_latency_ms=120; prewarm disabled in base runs, and a prewarm variant where sessions are pinned for 60s.
- Metrics: p50/p95 latency (end-to-end), tokens/sec per GPU, DPQ (dollars per query) estimated from infra amortized cost numbers (internal table), and warm-hit rate (KV cache effective reuse).

Raw observations (annotated numbers):
Table: mean tokens/session vs p95 and DPQ (Model-A on single A100, burst windows of 30s at 120 qps sustained during window).
- mean_tokens: 4 -> p50: 82ms, p95: 310ms, DPQ: $0.016
- mean_tokens: 12 -> p50: 130ms, p95: 240ms, DPQ: $0.022
- mean_tokens: 48 -> p50: 190ms, p95: 260ms, DPQ: $0.045

Interpretation: when sessions are extremely short (4 tokens), p95 blows up due to slot churn and cold-start penalty; DPQ is lower than medium sessions because tokens/sec is dominated by many small calls but higher tail amplifies perceived latency SLO failures. Medium sessions (12 tokens) hit a “sweet spot” where batching amortizes kernel startup and reduces tail; long sessions push model compute and increase DPQ.

ASCII sparklines: p95 latency across mean_tokens = [4,12,48] (Model-A @ A100)
- p95: ░░░▒████ (4 -> 310ms)
- p95: ░░▒███▒░░ (12 -> 240ms)
- p95: ░▒██░░░░░ (48 -> 260ms)

Throughput vs latency mosaic (burst window snapshot):
We capture a 30s burst window and plot tokens/sec (avg) vs p95 measured over sliding 5s windows. Below is a compact text mosaic where each column is a 5s window (0..5), (5..10), ..., (25..30). Numbers are tokens/sec / p95-ms.
- window0: 850 tps / 320ms | window1: 920 tps / 305ms | window2: 1100 tps / 270ms | window3: 1020 tps / 290ms | window4: 470 tps / 210ms | window5: 240 tps / 190ms
Note: early windows show higher p95 due to simultaneous arrival of many new sessions; middle window benefits from batching stabilization; tail windows drop as burst subsides and KV cache warms in medium sessions.

A100 vs H100: delta sketch (Model-A, mean_tokens=12):
- A100 p95: 240ms, DPQ: $0.022
- H100 p95: 180ms, DPQ: $0.027
Trade: H100 reduces tail by ~25% at the cost of higher amortized hourly GPU price, so DPQ increases for medium/long sessions. However for very latency-sensitive SLOs (p50 target <100ms), H100 unlocks that band whereas A100 requires aggressive prewarm or lower concurrency.

Prewarm effect (60s pinning) summary (Model-B, sparse mix):
- prewarm enabled: p95 dropped from 310ms -> 150ms for mean_tokens=4 but DPQ increased by ~18% due to occupied slots during idle periods.
- prewarm is a deterministic lever: good for high-value customers/SLA tiers; bad for PLG low-usage traffic.

Meters and amortization example (internal cost assumptions used):
- price assumptions used for DPQ: A100-hour equivalent: $2.40/hr (amortized infra + ops); H100-hour equivalent: $6.90/hr. Node utilization measured as token-throughput normalized across model size. These are simplified for the memo; see linked spreadsheet for full amortization.

Micro-annotations & hypotheses (what's surprising / worth chasing):
1) Fragmentation cliffs: when mean_tokens < 6, small-session churn causes slot fragmentation—observed p95 spikes from concurrent session creation/teardown. This is consistent with the tiling/batching inefficiency note we saw elsewhere but is more pronounced under Poisson bursts.
2) KV cache has diminishing returns for very short sessions; most reuse occurs only after medium-length conversations (>=12 tokens).
3) H100 helps tail but is not cost-effective for high-volume low-SLA traffic. Consider hybrid routing: keep A100 for default tier, route premium low-latency flows to H100 (or prewarmed pools).
4) Prewarm as a paid feature: clear tradeoff between latency and blankslot cost. Potential to expose a “prewarm window” billing/option in Dedicated offering.

Visual/text figure: p95 vs DPQ curve (concise points)
- point1: (mean_tokens=4) -> (p95=310ms, DPQ=$0.016)
- point2: (mean_tokens=12) -> (p95=240ms, DPQ=$0.022)
- point3: (mean_tokens=48) -> (p95=260ms, DPQ=$0.045)
Observational note: DPQ is not strictly monotonic with p95; the dominant factor is tokens-per-session which changes batching efficiency.

Recommendations (short):
- Product: surface an option for "session pinning / prewarm" as a Dedicated add-on; show clear DPQ delta in the console (preview cost vs latency).
- Runtime: evaluate a lightweight fast-path for ultra-short sessions that minimizes slot lifecycle overhead (thin RPC preamble + ephemeral microcontainers?). Prototype as a small traceable experiment behind a feature flag.
- Capacity planning: for customers with >50% sessions <8 tokens, provision slot oversubscription heuristics and cap concurrency to reduce p95 spikes rather than trying to flatten with H100.

Next steps / open questions:
- Run same set on multimodal small-image workloads (similar session sparsity) to validate cross-modality behavior.
- Formalize the amortization spreadsheet into a console estimator for DPQ by session-profile.
- Microbenchmark: instrument slot create/destroy path to identify top 3 hotspots contributing to the 30-120ms startup penalty observed in short-session p95.

Appendix: small experiment log (timestamps)
- 2027-05-07 09:12 - baseline run Model-A @ A100 (no prewarm) - 30s bursts x 10 windows
- 2027-05-07 11:03 - Model-B comparative run @ H100 (no prewarm)
- 2027-05-08 08:20 - prewarm=60s runs (A100 & H100)
- 2027-05-10 15:44 - follow-up micro-profiling to capture slot creation latency (trace ids in linked PR)

Notes to self (informal):
- store the full timeseries in bench/sparse-output/2027-05-07/ and link in the playbook.
- prioritize creating a small dashboard tile in console that maps session distribution -> expected DPQ at p50/p95 so solutions eng can show customers live tradeoffs.

End.
